eqy_routed.scope: whole flat routed netlist vs flattened RTL. The routed netlist has no hierarchy, so the Part 1 split is applied by name: 16 per-PE partitions, each = the 32 acc_o bits of one PE with accumulator register + INT8 multiplier + 32-bit adder + clear/valid gating (i.e. 'mac_int8 incl. multiplier', proven 16 times, cut at the operand/valid registers), plus the wrapper partitions (skew registers, operand registers, valid delay line, busy). Operand/skew/valid registers correspond by net name, accumulators by the output port bit they drive

scope_exact.cell_models: nangate45 cell functions from NangateOpenCellLibrary_typical.lib of the pinned ORFS image (path and sha256 in inputs)
scope_exact.cut_points: operand registers (a_q, b_q), skew registers (a_sr, b_sr), valid delay line, primary inputs
scope_exact.gate: flat routed netlist 6_final.v (one module, no mac_int8 hierarchy), sha256 in inputs.routed_netlist_sha256
scope_exact.kind: zero-delay logical (sequential, x-propagating) equivalence per partition; not a timing check
scope_exact.partitions: 27 = 16 per-PE cones (accumulator register + 8x8 signed multiplier + 32-bit adder + clear/valid gating, i.e. mac_int8 including the multiplier, once per PE) + 11 wrapper partitions (a_sr, b_sr, a_q, b_q register banks, 6 valid taps, busy)
scope_exact.register_correspondence: 806 flops matched by name: operand, skew and valid registers by the RTL name on their Q net; the 512 accumulator bits by the output port bit they drive (acc_o[32*(4*i+j)+b]), since the router renamed their Q nets

The cell models do parse in Verilator, so the Verilator half of the task is NOT done when its simulation was not run: gls_routed_pass = true then means 'the Icarus gate-level simulation passes', a partial fulfilment of item 4, not a two-simulator result
